utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, may I invite you to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The -- we were informed that the Defence wanted to raise a preliminary matter. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to respond to -- actually, request to explain our objections to the P07527. It's Official Note composed by AID on 12th of April, 2000, and in that official report, AID is addressing the interview with Mr. Bilcar, Dusan, conducted on 10th of April, 2000 regarding the death of his wife, Ratke Bilcar. From this document, it is not visible to who this official report is addressed, is not visible who composed this report. There is no number, or case or number or protocol under which case is recorded. And there is no this interview attached to the document although it was mentioned that the interview was conducted. So those are basically our objections to this document. And another thing we would -- we should shortly go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. In relation to P7527, because that's what we started with, any response or any further submissions to be made on this Official Note?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not at the moment, Mr. President, although I had -- I mean, if obliged to do so, I would have a couple of preliminary submissions. But I would prefer, if the Court doesn't mind, to give us an opportunity to review the quick history of the tendering of this document and then get back to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Within the next two days, would that be sufficient, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll hear from you within two days. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We are calling Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, perhaps I briefly ask your attention for D1211. You had asked that -- that Svetlana Radovanovic's expert report, you had asked certain pages to be verified as to the accuracy of its translation. Now, the report was the translation on all these pages were accurate. Nevertheless you agreed uploading a new -- a new translation so the Chamber wonders and would like to hear from you why, if the accuracy was confirmed, why there nevertheless is a new translation. So if would you inform us about that rather soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, you are now in a different position compared to where we've seen you for a while. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Poparic. Please be seated. It may be clear to you now that your role now changed from advising the Defence to being a witness, an expert witness, who has a different role. You are aware of that, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic -- well, I usually say you finds him to your left but you know that he's there. And what Mr. Lukic is, that is, that he's counsel for Mr. Mladic may not come as a surprise to you either. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, kindly state your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: I am Mile Poparic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you draft an expert report for of the purposes of Mladic Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I created several reports in co-operation with my colleague, Mrs Zorica Subotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens 1D05499, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a document on the screen before you. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in the creation of this expert report?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the report require any changes or amendments?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Basically, there's nothing. There's just one thing, but perhaps we can deal with it later when we get to that point and then I'll specify the error. As for the rest, and as far as I could see, it is correct. Perhaps there is the odd small mistake here and there, but nothing of significance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we are not offering this at this moment anyways, I will come back to those corrections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, I will continue with my questions now and then we can turn to the corrections later on. In 2013, did you testify in a case?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I testified in the case against Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since that time, did you gain any new insights in the incidents you discussed in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because of these new insights, did you change your report with regard to any incidents dealt with in the Karadzic case significantly?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: No, things were not changed, but we simply tried to define a particular incident more precisely. For example, incident F-8 of the 8th of October, incident F-16 of the 3rd of March, 1995, as well as a couple of other cases, where we were able to define it more precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look, then, at F-16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document, it is page 232 in the B/C/S and 239 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you were drafting this report and the Karadzic report, how did you acquire the necessary information about the incidents?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: We received most of that information from Mr. Karadzic's Defence. Later on, we received some from you, and that was the bulk of the information contained. However, there were cases where not everything was defined or there were contradictory pieces of information in existence. Hence, it was highly useful to obtain as much information as possible, and we tried in different ways to acquire that information. We also relied on the website of the Tribunal and various other websites where we could get some information about certain events, including footage and so on. We were also in contact with the people involved and so on and so forth. We tried hard to acquire as much information as possible, so as to be able to define the cases as precisely as possible. However, I have to say that there were about two incidents where we were unable to say explicitly it happened this or that way because the information about the incidents is contradictory. We did not have a defined threshold to screen the information and to say, This is correct and that is incorrect. Perhaps we would require -- or this Bench will require some additional information obtained through some other witnesses in order to be able to assess it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what were the basic problems you encountered in drafting this, the fourth report, the report pertaining to small-arms?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: With incidents involving small-arms, traces are always a problem because the location is quickly changed. The people involved leave, and they there are no significant traces left of the there may be some small ones that need to be registered immediately. It frequently happened that it was not the case, and the police did not register all such traces. That was one thing. Another thing, all these cases are frequently tied to injury and it is crucial that there is forensic documentation on file, but in most of the cases, it was non-existent. There were some cases where there were doctors' reports, specifying the location of injury, but always quite limited in terms of information. That was one problem with these cases. There was a problem with police information as well, because it often proved unreliable particularly in terms of the place of incident. For example, we had cases where there was a distance of up to 200 metres between the place of incident specified and what we find in the report. For example, the 1st of November, 1995 incident, that case is not scheduled in the indictment. There is an incident of the 23rd of November. However, the previous case was discussed in the Milosevic case and it was specified that the incident took place close to the Holiday Inn and the Metalka building and the judgement contains that information. However, I received from you a ballistics report signed by Emir Turkusic and Edin Suljic [phoen], if I were to go by the initials on the document. It is specifically stated in at that document that the tram was in the Zmaja od Bosne street which is always 300 metres away from the place of incident indicated in the judgement. I don't know how it came about that that piece of information was missing in the Milosevic case. Also, in the same incident, the police in their reports stated that the incident took place as specified in the indictment and then the same police force puts a different piece of information in their other report. There were other such cases. For example, there is the case of Miljenka Cvitkovica Street where a boy had been wounded. All information pointed to Miljenka Cvitkovica Street but the on-site investigation and all evidence comes from Dzemala Bijedica Street which is a different street. So that was one of the biggest problems. Another problem, as I said, was the lacking forensic documentation, which in some cases was crucial. And in cases such as those we were unable to determine anything specifically. There was also a problem with the Prosecution asserting that an incident took place at a different location such as the case of the 27th of February, 1995, which, beyond dispute, happened in front of the Museum of the Revolution and the Prosecution asserted and Barry Hogan took footage with a witness indicating that it also happened at an intersection in front of the Metalka building. There was a witness testifying --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: When I testified in the Karadzic case, the Prosecution showed me a photograph allegedly taken from the Faculty of Theology and it was very important to be specific about the case. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to recognise the photograph and what was depicted because it was zoomed in. Later on, after my testimony, I received the photograph and I could see immediately that it wasn't accurate. There was a whole set of photographs whereby I established that wasn't taken from the school of theology but from a building next door which was under construction at the time and the photograph was taken from the scaffolding. From the school of theology that place is not visible. One could not take a photograph from there because of a crown of a tree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we've now heard for three pages an overall assessment of the whole of the case, the judgements delivered, comment on matters, photographs, that could not be taken from point A or from point B. We understand that this witness had certain problems, and we invite you to get back to the expertise of this witness, what he could tell us, and this witness is not here to give his overall assessment of both -- all of the evidence before us or not before us, to give his overall assessment of the quality of our judgements. You know that there's an Appeals Chamber who could deal with that. And let's get back to what the witness is here for; that is, to tell us what his expertise can bring us, and then, please, in concrete terms and not in general sweeping statements. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the gentleman gave us exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I invited you to proceed, not to comment on what I said. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand this sweeping statements. Is it a sweeping statement when he gives the exact address --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you don't understand me. That's a pity. But I think my invitation [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... What you don't understand the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we're not in a debate. You can put the next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, when you refer to the particular addresses in the city, are they also referred to in your reports as well as in our indictment?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you use newspaper reports?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had the opportunity of seeing film footage, TV reports of war reporters, and that was very useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why do you think it was useful and why did you use newspaper reports?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Well, as regards small-arms fire, according to the indictment, it is alleged that citizens were exposed to constant sniper fire, especially at cross-roads in streets where they moved about, et cetera. There are quite a few newspaper reports to that effect. These reports attracted my attention because I noticed that in quite a few reports there is a reference to cross-roads, intersections where people are running across some intersection and one can see that there's some kind of danger. However, in some footage I saw some illogical things, for example, people lying by the intersection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I asked you to get to concrete matters. Newspaper articles, are they in evidence? Can we look at them?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please go to what you want to, that is, concrete information about incidents rather than all kind of background information which we do not know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see video that is marked as 1D05925. And we'll see the time-frame from 1 hour, 51 minute, 32 seconds to 1 hour, 51 minute, 54 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we also know what incident we are talking about. Is it one of the Scheduled Incidents in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is in connection with testimony of Mr. Van Lynden. I don't know if I pronounce his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Van Lynden. Okay, what part of his testimony so that we know what we are going to look at and we can have a focussed look on what we see before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can find this in the report of Mr. Poparic and Ms. Subotic. We'll first see the video and then I'll go to the report, and we'll have some questions in connection with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you already tell us where you will take us later, so at least we can have a look at the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's page 37 in English version, figure 8. Of 1D5499. Can we see the video now. Can we start, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now if we can go to 1D05499, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Mr. Poparic, what was depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Fire in a residential building in the street Zmaja od Bosne, which is close Marin Dvor, so it is close to the centre. It was taken by Van Lynden, a reporter from Sky News, and in his report he claimed that this building had been hit with incendiary bullets --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could all another microphones be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see something is falling, and it's incendiary ammunition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can help us to recognise the object falling? I can't see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could enlarge the photographs. Where do we see it. Which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it would be useful if I were to mark it using a marker, so that it would be easier for you to fall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would first tell us what of the six photographs we should look at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] See here? We're looking at all the photographs A through D, that is to say, A, B, C, D. These are segments that follow the trajectory of this object. On slide A, in the upper left-hand corner, we see this object that is alight, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in only on A, B, C and D. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you wish I can mark it. So here on slide A, this object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no markings without being invited to do so. If you would start telling us what you draw our attention to. And are you at --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Slide A, you said, on slide A, the upper left-hand corner, we see this object that is alight. Do you mean in the upper left-hand corner of A --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would wait until I finish --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you would wait until I finish my question, because there's no way you can taken not knowing what my question will be. Photograph A, is the left upper photograph. What were you drawing our attention to in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm indicating this object that is alight and it is underneath this window in the upper left-hand corner. It's a bit below. It's a bit below the window. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Perhaps if would be good if the witness marks that with the assistance of the usher. Because at this moment I do not see something in the upper left-hand corner which is alight. Could you mark on photograph A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll mark it with a number 1. That is position 1 of that object. I drew this line a bit over that object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be -- could it be rubbed out again so that can you do it around it, so that we could still see it. Mr. Usher, could you assist in removing the little circle so that the witness can now put the circle around and perhaps again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now, again, you put a 1 next to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And say that's a light object. Yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say this is alight or did you say it's a light object. On the record I read that you said it was alight and I want to understand how you make the determination that it's alight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Physically, it's burning. We saw that in the film footage. It's burning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't see the burning. The burning I see from the window. There, I see a red dot and I don't know whether it is alight or something else and I don't see whether -- I don't see whether it's burning, that's why I'm asking you how you make those determinations. How do you see it's burning and how do you know it's alight. I see a dot, a red dot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be seen very nicely in the film footage, if you look at it carefully. We can play it again. As it is falling, it has a kind of flame and Van Lynden is also claiming that it's on fire, the man who was there. It fell in front of him. And he claims that it is on fire. That it's aflame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, maybe we should see the footage then. Because as a still I just see a dot. I don't see what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you start with further explaining to us what we see here that we look again after that to see the video to see whether we can ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we look at slide B that object has a position that's a bit different. It's further up. See? Number 2. So when we look at it in relation to the window it is higher up. In relation to the position in photograph A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next slide, C, I'll mark it with number 3, this object is perhaps a bit above this, but this is where it reaches its maximum in terms of height. And let us move on to slide D now. Here, it is already falling. It is descending. So let that be number 4. So that is how it falls. Well, we can't see it anymore. Then it hits the ground and then bounces off, say, 2 metres, and then falls somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you know that the Chamber would like --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To see the video again, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- To look at it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll try and pause and play it in a very fast sequence so, still, we'll have it a bit longer on our screens because it's very fast. So can we play the video again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First, tender this marked photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once it is removed from the screen, it's lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we tender this marked versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the marked version is the marked version which contains only four out of the six photographs which were in the original and the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1325, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we start, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it any use for us first to look at the lower two photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stop. Okay. Continue, continue. Stop. Continue. Stop. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, in your view, how was this flame created? Is it incendiary ammunition or what?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Mr. Van Lynden said that it's incendiary ammunition and that the JNA had incendiary ammunition in its equipment. That is only partly true. In the JNA, there was one bullet, 20-millimetre calibre. It was called an incendiary bullet, armour piercing. It had a steel top and then there was this mix that would be set on fire once it hits the surface. I can also draw a sketch of this, if it would be useful for the Trial Chamber. And if this projectile impacts - this is basically anti-aircraft ammunition - then this pyrotechnical mix is set on fire because of the pressure and then it sets off a spark and then that is supposed to set something on fire, say, fuel. So it's a few grams, and it just creates a blaze. The entire projectile cannot be set on fire. So it doesn't look like this. So this is not that particular ammunition. Secondly, the trajectory of this object cannot be a projectile. Certainly not. Because we see here that it goes underneath one window, reaches another window, say, a metre and a half, and then it falls on the ground. That would mean that this projectile had ricocheted which certainly could not have happened in this case. There could have been a ricochet only if it hit the building at a smaller angle, less than 20 degrees, and then there could have been a ricochet and then it could have moved along the length of the building. It certainly couldn't have fallen underneath the building in this way. It is a metal object because it can be heard that it bounced off. Also, a metal object where there was some cloth or something, I don't know, say, you can just use crude oil and throw it through the window. The trajectory we see here, matches that. For example, you set this on fire, you throw it up, and then it goes up about a metre and a half and then falls down. This is obviously something --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, we can no longer hear the witness. There are too many microphones on and there is a lot of background noise. We apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question to the witness. You told us a lot about your conclusions and -- but you didn't specify where you got the details from. Was it only taken the details, the factual details, from this video we have seen and the photographs, the stills, or do you have any additional sources?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The facts I presented about ammunition, that came from other sources. That has to do with recognition of ammunition. However, the flame itself, the torch, that is a conclusion on the basis of this film, and that is sufficient. So if you look at it, it can be played once again. If you look at how it falls. It bounces off. We see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This was not my question. I just wanted to know the source where you draw your -- where you based your conclusions on, that was so -- with respect to this object. This is only the video. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was only based on the footage and my knowledge of the characteristics of the projectile. I know very well when ricochet can occur --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this is your knowledge. That's fine. But you didn't see, personally, this piece on flames which was falling down? You didn't see that and you don't have any additional knowledge about this artefact. Is it true -- is that correct?

utterances.text: But can we save this one. I don't know if we would be able to stop on this point again. And then if you want, we can go back.
