utterances.text: Is there any technical way of having that sequence of approximately 1 or 2 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1 second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To split it up and have a full still of every single position where you can stop so that you see the line, you see the first development of the smoke, perhaps even the development of the line, and then how the smoke or whatever it is, then further --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not have technical means unless going step by step manually. So I don't know if the Prosecution has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if there's -- but there's no reason to not at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Try it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- admit this already. And then if we could have -- if technical assistance could be given by the Prosecution to have every single step --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honours, we would have to do it manually. We don't have any kind of programme or facilities to be able to do it. We would be doing the same way my friend would be doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Lukic you're invited to do that. But we start already with this still, the first one we had already. We had a number reserved for this, and now for this still.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives exhibit number D1327.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we are waiting for it to be uploaded. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move on in the same manner, step by step. Can we play it actually until 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stop. And, again, go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Ah, too late. We saw something as well. Go further. No -- let's go further and, then, we'll go back. Can we stop here. There's another trace at 1 hour, 51 minutes, 41 seconds. Everything is in 41 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that here it is going through the smoke and cuts off, if I can say so, the lower right lower part -- the right lower part. It goes approximately from the middle of the bottom to, I would say, 70 per cent up to the right of the -- in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This one we have saved in the report of Mr. Poparic. It's figure 9 from his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And one before that, that we just missed. We didn't stop in time. So if we go to figure 9, it's page 39 of English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The left of the two -- the right of the two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The right one that we have -- had on our screens in that video. And the left one is what we saw just fragment of a second before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, in your view, the stills you took from the footage depicted in image 9, does it show outgoing or incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: It is outgoing fire. And to repeat once again, this kind of trajectory could not have been achieved from VRS positions. If it had come from VRS positions, it would have been far more horizontal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no one has asked you yet, I think, from what positions they were fired. The simple question was whether it was incoming fire or outgoing fire. And incoming fire may come from whatever positions. Have you considered that? Because apparently your conclusion depends on your analysis of who would have fired it from where; whereas, from a ballistic point of view, I think if you exclude that question, could you tell us on the basis of what you see here, whether it's incoming or outgoing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is outgoing fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On what basis from what we see here can you tell us that it's outgoing? We don't see the origin at -- for neither of the two, or do we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It cannot be seen because it is covered by the screen of smoke. But you can see the trace being created, just on the basis of the still itself, we cannot see it. But if you look at the footage carefully you can see it, although it is very fast.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not understand the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last sentence of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the photograph itself, one cannot conclude the source of fire but on the footage, we can see that it is outgoing fire. What I said about the trajectory it further solidifies my opinion when I claim that is outgoing fire. There were no positions on either the ABiH or VRS side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We've heard that. What we're doing at this moment is to focus exclusively on what we see in this footage, which you commented on. Is there anything we should specifically look at apart from whether we see it moving in one direction or another? Is there any other aspect which we should focus on when, again, looking at this footage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only if we focus on the way the trace was created, to the extent possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we look at it once again. Mr. Lukic, if you then have any further questions, please put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should we look at it once again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to look at it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Interpose this as well, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that would be best.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are playing the video again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were you able to see whether the lines went up or down? Were you able to see that or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I could see, the lines were moving from the building upwards. And I've said that a number of times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest that we move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want to ask a question about this one. This line, sir, at the end of the picture at the bottom, it seems like it is still in the air. It hasn't reached the building. So I'm not quite sure how one determines where in the building it comes from, according to your argument that is an outgoing shot. Because we don't see, unlike the previous one that we looked at that, we saw that it hits on the wall, I don't see where it hits on the -- on this building for me to -- if I go according to your argument to say that that is the source. So how do you determine that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When looking at it, we need to look at the other trace which was far clearer and it came out of the building to the left near the balconies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm going to stop you. I'm not going to look at this and -- I'm looking at this one. I'm asking about this one. I'm saying this line goes through smoke which seems to be outside the building. We can see the building further on. And it ends on the photograph before it has reached the building. So I'm not sure whether it is -- I -- I'm not sure where from the building, if you say it comes from the building, where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It cannot be established based on the photograph because of the smoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... no, it's not because of the smoke. It's because of the direction of the line. The direction of the -- the photograph ends before this line hits the building, so I don't know where it comes from. And when I say where it comes from, I'm basing that question based on your argument that this is an outgoing bullet and not incoming. So where it comes from, I don't see. Can you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No photograph can show us that. We need to take the footage to see the continuity, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying if we continue this line we'll come back again and go to the source? We have gone past this line. If we continue, you're going to pass this line and I'm not seeing where this line comes from in relation to the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we were to extend the line, from this angle, we would definitely be able to reach the place of origin. But we can't do it on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That -- I can agree with that. But, unfortunately, this photograph doesn't take us to the origin of the thing. And that's my question. That's precisely my concern, that how can we accept this as saying it comes from the building when we don't even see how far it goes towards the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The footage is the only thing that's valid. This still was simply given to try and locate a position in the footage itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This still is a still in the footage. If you move from this still, you're not going to see this still again. So it -- the rest of the footage won't tell us where this line comes from, from the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The rest of the footage could show us the development of the line. That's the only thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just told you how impossible that is. You keep repeating the same story. Anyways. That's your answer. Thank you so much. As long as you can see that we can't see where it comes from --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also agree with you that it is impossible to do based on the photograph. But the traces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you agree with me, then I have no further questions thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one short question, and please try to focus on that one. What's the sense of firing into a huge smoke area with a bullet from a building which apparently has -- where you are in great danger to be because of the fire? Could you tell us what your -- whether you have given it any thought at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As I said, it's a dangerous spot. It is; that's true. But we cannot conclude here that the marksman is in smoke; right? Probably somewhere on the side, as was the case before, the big question is why it was fired there. It's hard to give an answer to that. Possibly fire had been opened from this building and then on the other side, they responded, and then the place was set on fire. That is realistic. Secondly, there were TV crews there. Now, what did somebody wish to film? Perhaps they wanted to see a building on fire and to film that. These are just assumptions. I cannot say. What really surprised me -- I mean, in my view, it is certainly that there was firing from that building and it is certain that Mr. Van Lynden said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear what Mr. Van Lynden said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, who did all the firing and who set the building on fire, that I have no way of knowing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, it is realistic that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: One last question. Sir, this is outgoing fire what would have been the target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I mean, I've just said that it's hard to say what the objective of the firing is. In my view, there are two possibilities; that somebody opened fire from this building and that there was a fire that came in response and that's how the building was set on fire. However, the presence of TV crews, journalists, maybe that created a necessity on somebody's part to have some firing filmed on this building. We shouldn't forget the object that was thrown. This was an effect. I mean, I'm not saying who set the building on fire. Maybe the building was on fire but somebody took advantage of the presence of the TV crew to create this propaganda impression with regard to this building. It is a very thankless thing for me to try to say what happened there, all the things that happened there. In my view, I've seen this thousands of times. And firing did come from this building. And I see that you have a problem also with ascertaining all of this. I mean, I looked at this for days and that is why I am saying with certainty that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes. Witness you are going far beyond the field of your expertise. Listen carefully to the next question that Mr. Lukic will put to you. We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only for the record, Your Honour, Mr. Van Lynden testifying in this case on the transcript page 1344, line 1, until transcript page 1345, line 1, claimed that this building was not used by Army of B and H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was claimed in our trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What has that got to do with what we just saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We think if it was proved that it was fired from that building, that the building was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I do understand that if you assume that this was outgoing fire and if it was assumed that it was ABiH fire, then you -- that would shed some doubt, perhaps over Mr. Van Lynden's, but that's a lot of presumptions. Let's move on. I invited you to put the next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D5499 on our screens again. Figure 9. So we had it before. English page 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The left-hand picture was taken -- actually, did you take both from the same video?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The one on the left, you can see clearly that it comes from the building --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not hear the end of the witness's answer. Could he please be asked to speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you come a bit closer to the microphone. And could you repeat the last part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph on the left, we took it from the same film. And it can be seen very nicely there that this is outgoing. It can be seen how it is coming into being. It is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask you something now about positions around Sarajevo, Mr. Poparic. So we need your paper in both versions, 1D5499. We need page 59 in B/C/S and page 55 in English. Figure 26. Photograph 26; that's what we'll be looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In figure 26, it says that it is from the area of Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You marked that using numbers as well. Were you in the area?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes, twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you establish the separation lines?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the remnants of trenches and communicating trenches, it was easy to determine where the positions of the ABiH were and where the positions of the VRS were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go to the page 60 in B/C/S - it's the next page - and next page in English as well, which is page 56. Now we need figure 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see image 27 before us. Who took these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: I most probably took these photographs. Maybe it was Mrs. Subotic, but I think it was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what do we see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: In photograph 28, on the left, we see the view of Spicasta Stijena from the other side. So if we were to go on looking straight ahead, there's Sarajevo. So this is the approaches to Spicasta Stijena and we see what these approaches are like. It's not a very good view. The copy is not very good and there is this communicating trenches all the way up to there. These were positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and at the front side of Spicasta Stijena. On the right, we see these rocks, and these were the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska at Spicasta Stijena. Well, cannot be seen very well, can it? Maybe it can be seen a bit better here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're going to move on. You explained to us what it was what you photographed. Now let us move on to image 30; page 61 in B/C/S and 57 in English. We see it very well. In the English version, we see image 29 as well, photograph 29. What is depicted in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: In image 30, we see positions of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is a panoramic photograph. That is to say, several photographs were taken. Because it's a very big area. And roughly in the middle, we see this path than is the path that separates Grdonj on the left and Spicasta Stijena on the right. However, the position of the BH army move right to Spicasta Stijena. It wasn't possible to show absolutely everything in this photograph. We can see that in photograph 29 on the right-hand side. We can see the view. The view of Spicasta Stijena, up hill. And the traces of these positions of the BH army can be seen there, some of these deep trenches and also the rocks piled up for communicating trenches. And also there are these shelters that were made at Grdonj, to the left, and to the right, is Spicasta Stijena. These positions at Spicasta Stijena went basically up to the top, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far away were the trenches and these fortified positions of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in relation to the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: These trenches were very close to the trenches of the Army of Republika Srpska. In my own estimate it is 20, 30 metres, I think that they literally could have talked to one another. There is this film that shows that's the way it was, an action taken by the Black Swans. That's a special unit of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They came from Tuzla. And they attacked the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. And it can be seen exactly where it was that they could have come from. That matches what I saw on the ground. I think that film was shown here when Witness Rasevic testified, Rasko, if I remember correctly, and it can be seen very well, the position of these trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] for the record -- yes, yes, I forgot to turn on my microphone. Thank you. For the record, in our case, that video is marked as D00553.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move on. Now I'd like to show you something else from this very same report of yours. Image 33. In B/C/S, it's page 64; in English, it is page 61.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can, only English version in front of us and only this figure with legend. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, many of the incidents that are in the indictment occurred in the area of Marin Dvor. Can you describe the characteristics of this area for us; and can you tell us how come you know?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: The separation lines at Marin Dvor were very complex and there are some very characteristic spots. These two lines, the red line and the blue line, denote the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of the BiH. They're blue. And between them is the Miljacka river. On the side of the Army of Republika Srpska in Grbavica there are these characteristic buildings. There is number 1, Metalka and the building number 4 -- sorry. Sorry. 14, it is these four white sky-scrapers. The indictment, the police documentation, most often mentioned these two facilities as sources of fire against civilian, trams and so on. The situation is so complex and that is shown by 2A and 2B that was one building divided into two parts. In 2A it was the BH army, whereas 2B was under the control of the VRS. That building was renovated so it still seems to be divided because half of it is one colour and the other half another colour. As for BH army, there's this characteristic building of 8, that is the BH Assembly. Then 9, BH Executive Council. And then in the back, there is this tall building, the Unis building. 11 is the Holiday Inn hotel. Then 12 is the technical school, where Pretis was during the war. That is to say, military production. And the most important building here is building number 13, that is the Marsal Tito barracks. It was torn down to a certain extent. The American embassy is there now. We can see the white sky-scrapers opposite the Marsal Tito barracks and sniper positions were found there after the Dayton Agreement when the VRS left this area, the police carried out an on-site investigation and photographs were taken, and that is where there were fortified sniper positions. The same is alleged for the Metalka building, but there was no proof that was ever provided, that there was a fortified sniper nest there. The police did not find that and nobody gave any concrete evidence of the existence of a sniper position there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question that has to do with Metalka. In how many cases did you establish that they were caused by sniper fire or other kinds of fire from the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: In all the cases that we looked at, we ascertained that not in a single case was fire from the Metalka the source or the cause. There was only this one case where we could not establish whether that had been the case or had not been the case. I've already told you at the beginning that there were such cases, but we will get to that as well, won't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time for our break now but I'm just going to ask you one more thing. These four sky-scrapers what is their link with the Marsal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: It's direct. As you can see, they're right opposite barracks and that's where the sniper positions were. And in my view it is logical that there would be sniper positions there. Any commander would put sniper positions there because that is how one controls the area of the barracks; right? I mean, that is only natural to take advantage of this kind of building for a sniper position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the break time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. The witness may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just one very small thing that I wanted to put on the record. I'm not completely sure that the small video-clips we were looking at today are all subsumed within P71 and I just wanted to note we'll look at it overnight, the time codes, to make sure that everything is there and if not we'll revert to you to see if we could get some extra small video-clips admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's very possible, Your Honour. That's why we didn't use P71, we used 65 ter -- the whole video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I take it that you appreciate that Ms. Edgerton will check so that we don't have unnecessary --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, we will now focus on the incidents scheduled in the indictment. I will start with F-1. In your report, which is 1D05499, we will need to see page 68 in both versions, item 18. [In English] Obviously in English version, we should go one page back. One more, sorry. One more. Yes, thank you. Page 65, English, I'm sorry. I had wrong page noted. [Interpretation] The incident happened on 13th of December, 1992 in Zagric Street. In the indictment it is stated that at house number 38, Anisa Pita a 3-year-old girl was injured to the leg. Did you manage to establish where the girl was when she was shot according to the documentation you had?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: According to the documents, she was at the entrance of her house taking off her shoes when a bullet hit her in the foot. In this image, at number 39, the door cannot be seen any longer because the low -- actually the wall with the yellow brick was constructed subsequently. At the time of incident, it wasn't there. And a door was there instead where the girl was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are recorded as saying number 39. I think it's number 38, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The house number is 38, but the image number is 39 in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, what is characteristic of this case, in your view?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: In this case, the basic problem was to establish whether that location was at all visible from Stijena Baba from which it was asserted she was shot at. Stijena Baba is some 900 metres away. Between the house and Stijena Baba, there are trees and buildings, as well as uneven terrain, and it was necessary to establish whether there was clear visibility. I also have to say that during the war the VRS positions were at Stijena Baba. They never went further down below. So we wanted to establish first whether the place was visible from there, whether the girl could be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll check that analysis. In your view, was the place where the girl was wounded visible from Baba Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now look at page 75 in your report in B/C/S -- or perhaps we can stay with the English version alone. And it is on page 72. We're interested in image 47. What can we see on this still from your report, image number 47, what does the left-hand side one depict and the right side?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: The left-hand side photograph was taken by Mr. Van der Weijden, an OTP expert. The right-hand side was taken by me. The difference is that Mr. Van der Weijden zoomed in by six times, as specified in his report, and I did not use any zoom. Later on, I zoomed in digitally on a particular piece of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you take the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: In September 2010. I think on the 17th or 18th September 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one second. For the transcript, I wanted to say that this photograph -- or which of these photographs -- well, you said the right-hand side was Mr. Van der Weijden's?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: The right-hand side photograph is Mr. Van der Weijden's; the left-hand side is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the right-hand side one was taken from an exhibit in this case, and it is P01130, under seal, page 20 in the B/C/S and 15 in the English, photograph number 2. Let's look at -- well, do you want to say anything else in order to compare these two photographs?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The two photographs were taken from approximately the same place. Mr. Van der Weijden claimed he took his photograph from the entrance but in this case, I don't see how he could have ended up with this photograph since there are two wire fences in between. I don't know how he managed to take the photograph without the fences being seen. I took my photograph in front of the first fence at a slanted angle, if a line was drawn between the point and the door which was behind me by some 5 or 6 metres. Apart from that, the two photographs are basically identical. Mr. Van der Weijden asserted, and he marked it on the right photograph, that this outcrop of rock is Baba Stijena. As I mentioned, he took his photograph somewhat later in the year, in late November, when there was less vegetation. On my photograph, that part is slightly visible but more covered in green. It was probably grass. He asserted that it was Baba Stijena, and I claim it is not because it looks quite differently and is much further away from the location shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we next look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we move to another part of the transcript or an exhibit, on the left photograph, Witness, you indicate a house. Where can we see a house there. Can you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you explain that a bit further? I don't see a house. Or can we enlarge the left photograph. Is that a house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are some houses there, as you can see on a photograph taken from a distance. It is true that this photograph was zoomed in, and I can just make out the outline of a house. It has the shape of a house. On the photograph that can be seen in the report, we can see that there are houses in that part, in the direction of Stijena Baba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You're indicating a house, not houses. Are you telling us that the bended -- are you telling us that the bended line is part of a house or the structure inside of this line, below this line? What is the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The house is encircled. It is in the red line, and I'm talking about the only house we can see in this photograph. However, there are other houses in the area as can be seen from another photograph, although I don't know the number exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please answer only my questions. I'm not talking about other houses, only to understand this photograph. I asked you about the house you indicated. And you say it was -- "the house is encircled." Who did the encirclement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. It's so easy to answer these questions. Thank you so much. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought maybe Judge Orie has more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He's studying very thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm carefully looking at the evidence. You put the questions to the witness. I prefer that, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have page 66 only in this English version, please. We need image 41, the lower image, just to be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, can you explain what it is that we see this in photograph and what would be important for us to note?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: It is the -- a photograph of the area, including, Zagric Street and Stijena Baba taken from the Grdonj area, which is on the other side of Sarajevo. The resolution of the photograph is poor, though. However, we can make out Stijena Baba just to see what it looks like. We also have a red -- a yellow square depicting the word "shooter" which is where a trench of the VRS was. Just above that, we have a piece of rock that had been cut into the mountain, and, as shown, that is the Stijena Baba. We can see how big it is, and it is quite different from the outcrop marked by Mr. Van der Weijden. I think the difference is obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness is talking about the difference. I'm not what sure what this Stijena Baba, what is it being compared to. If we can see the two things --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Two image on -- on -- image 47 if you want to go back. We saw 4. Yes. Can we have then English page 47 -- 72, excuse me. English page 72.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you mean image 42 or page 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Image 47, page 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard what Judge Moloto was interested in.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand picture, Mr. Van der Weijden marked with an arrow this Stijena Baba in the terrain and it's much smaller and the shape is different compared to Stijena Baba on the picture on the right, 47.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Stijena Baba on the left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it cannot be seen. No, no, no, not this one. No. The right hand part of that picture. Yes. More. Now it says Stijena Baba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. I have seen what is being compared.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we should go shortly into the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D05499 on our screens again, please. We need page 71. And we need image 45 enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we see this. Actually what do we see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: In this photograph, we see the position of the building or, rather, the house in Zagric Street, number 38. This is Google Earth and we see the position of Stijena Baba, or rather the place where the firing position of the Army of Republika Srpska was. In relation to what was mentioned previously, we see that road depicted in that photograph. It would be this, here. Roughly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Getting to the arrow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness says "it's here," I am unable to follow him because I don't know what he points at. Therefore, Mr. Lukic, if you want us to understand that, then you have to either to ask the witness to mark it or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That would be the fastest way, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With the help of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you please make very clear what the witness exactly is marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So do tell us it is that you're marking and mark it with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: I'll mark the road that I said is in the lower right-hand corner. It's what we saw in the photograph of Mr. Van der Weijden's report. So it would be this road here. And I'll mark it with the number 1. This yellow arrow corresponds basically to the Zagric Street. And since the scale is large, this is Zagric number 2, and it my view, Mr. Van der Weijden marked it as being here, 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you, there's one part of this picture where it's zoomed in. Now, wouldn't it be clearer that you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... on the zoomed in portion if that is possible, if it is not possible --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the zoomed-in portion is just the surroundings of the building. It cannot be seen. So it's ... I mean, I think it cannot be seen there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'm trying to understand then what exactly it is that you zoomed in on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I zoomed in in order to determine where the house is in Zagric 38. And then on that basis, I drew this line. You see this line here? It is actually the zoomed-in part. The red line. In the zoomed-in part. From Stijena Baba to Zagric. So it's the same part and just this part that has been enlarged, so that it can be seen clearly how far it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And does the street you are indicating, does that not appear on the zoomed-in part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. It's further up. That's what I've been saying. What I marked with the number 3, that is roughly the area that Mr. Van der Weijden identified as the location of the house. It's a bit further down. Not a bit further down, but it's about 50 metres, in my estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we introduce this marked image into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives exhibit number D1328, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And another question related to this incident, Mr. Poparic. What is your final conclusion regarding this incident?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: My final conclusion is that the girl was not visible from Stijena Baba and she could not have been targeted intentionally at that moment, from Stijena Baba. She certainly was not targeted intentionally at all. Now where the bullet had come from, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just once again. You mentioned it but I don't know whether it's been recorded, all of it. Were there any natural obstacles between Stijena Baba and the place where she was?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: When we look at these photographs, there were all sorts of things. In order to be as sure as possible, but you know it's very hard to say, I was there twice and I never managed to see all this. However, in order to be sure I carried out analysis that is provided here. Using a topographical map and a profile of the terrain from Google Earth, an American map, a topographical map, that is, and a topographical map of the Yugoslav People's Army. In all three cases, I got results that were almost identical; the configuration of the terrain is such that the house in Zagrica 38 is not visible from there. So this showed that it's not visible. There's not a single -- I mean, even if there were not a single house or a single tree there, again, that spot would not have been visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you determine the visibility on the basis of a topographical map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I could establish whether there are any obstacles in the terrain itself. So let us disregard what is on the terrain, forest, houses, et cetera. I just looked at the terrain itself on the basis of topographical maps. According to all three of the sources, the terrain is such that there is this elevation of 2 or 3 metres in one place that conceals this house. It is very steep terrain and that's how it is possible to be this way. The results are very similar in all three cases, and that's why I believe they are reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we shortly see page 76 and we need image 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said I don't know where the bullet has come from, but not from Stijena Baba. I see in image 42 that you identify a place of a shooter which suggests that you know where the bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do know it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. No. I identified the position where the VRS was. That's where they were from the beginning to the end of the war. I visited that place, and it is visible to this day. Now, what is it that I'm asserting? That he could not have seen this little girl and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I just want to know what on image 42 the location "shooter" means. That's what I want to know. Perhaps we can have a look at it. It's page 67 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll explain. Since it is being alleged that the girl was hit from Stijena Baba, I proceeded from that, that the shooter who hit her was there. But then I established that he could not have seen her. Now, whether he was firing along a trajectory that's a parabola or something, I cannot say. But according to the documentation I had available, there was some fighting going on at the time. Now whether the bullet ricocheted somewhere or whatever, that I cannot say, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, what does "shooter" indicate. It's apparently not Stijena Baba. What did you depict where you said "shooter"? What stands that location for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means that that is where the presumed shooter was, the one who shot the girl. That's what we proceeded from, that he was there, that he fired at the girl. We are trying to ascertain whether he could have seen the girl. There's no denying that the VRS was there throughout the war. I assume that that's where he was. I'm not denying that. But then I ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, that's where you think the shooter may have been because he couldn't have been on Baba Stijena because he couldn't see the girl from there. And is that, then, the position from where you could have seen the girl and where the shooter presumably has been? Is that -- I just have -- don't understand exactly what you want to tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, from that spot, there was no visibility and that's where the position of the VRS was and it's quite visible to this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's still not an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you mean by this indication "shooter" the location according to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, according to the indictment. That's what they alleged, that that's where the fire came from and I proceeded from that fact and I analysed everything from there. I visited the spot, analysed the terrain and so on and I came to the conclusion that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this is not a possible location of a shooter, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But may I then ask you, where you point at "shooter," is that the same as Baba Stijena or is that a different location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It is -- I mean, it's that rock, Stijena Baba. If you look at number 42, down there, it's very steep and then the top of this rock, that's where the position was. Where it says "shooter." That is the top of the rock, the top of Stijena Baba, and it is very high up, like 20 metres high. You can see it in image 42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at it, but it is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, I can mark it so that it is clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The locations "shooter" and location Stijena Baba, are they identical in your view or are these different locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are identical. It's just that the location where the shooter was is a micro location. The shooter was at the top of Stijena Baba. Perhaps it would be useful if I marked what I believe to be Stijena Baba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- I think that's clear to me now. But what does you make believe that the indictment puts the shooter not on the top of Stijena Baba but on a point close to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There's misunderstanding about the top. Perhaps you are confused by the marking. Stijena Baba is above the road. The shooter was on the top of Baba Stijena, in my view. What you see behind is a road and the rock was created artificially. No one could have climbed up that way. There's a photograph, perhaps it isn't the best, but it might assist. It is photograph 40. Can you see the road and on the right-hand side Stijena Baba, where the VRS position was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it the two arrows from the rectangle "shooter" and the rectangle Stijena Baba are pointing, if I look at it, to different locations. But do I understand you correctly that you wanted to show that the shooter was exactly at the same location as the top of Stijena Baba? And, again, the shooter, according to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. The shooter was at this position. That's where he was supposed to be according to the indictment. The Stijena Baba marked above the road has no access path. It just a rock, sheer rock. Stijena Baba actually begins just below the shooter box. It is actually an abyss, some 20 metres deep, and that is Stijena Baba, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just briefly see image 50 on page 76.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly tell us what you wanted to show here.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: It's what I discussed when I talked about the lie of the land. It was done based on a topographic map created by the Military Mapping Institute in Belgrade. Based on the map, this profile was created, depicting the land between Zagric Street and Stijena Baba. If you draw a line between Zagric Street number 38 and Stijena Baba, at 483 metres, I believe, the slope actually goes over the line by some 2 metre, I think. We did something similar --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next photograph which is image 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] It's on the next page, 77.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did the same thing with an American map here. It is the same exercise I did with the -- previously with the Yugoslav military map. We see there's a slight difference because the point occurs at 387 metres where the outcrop is preventing the view. That is on the left-hand side. On the right-hand side, it is created by using Google Earth which did it automatically, and the height is 4.2, according to Google Earth. It may well be a bit more correct than the other two maps. In any case, it all fits well into the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you: What elevation from the ground level you took from exactly where the girl may have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to these photographs, the end point is Zagric Street number 38. That is where the girl was and the house --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But there is -- there's a house. You can take the roof of the house. You can take the foundation of the house. You can take the terrace of the house -- would you please not interrupt me. Yes. So what exactly did you take there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You saw the house on the photograph. It is picture 38. The entrance -- no, it wasn't 38. It was somewhere at the beginning. 39. The girl was about -- some 1 metre above ground where the gate is. There are two steps in between. So I suppose she was at about 1 metre from the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what did you -- at the other side, did you take the level or did you add 1 metre and a half for a standing-up person? How did you exactly measure where Baba Stijena is. You say it's all steep. So one metre further up could make a difference of half a metre or down. How did you exactly determine those positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We determined the positions by taking -- well, I didn't take into account the possibility that the shooter climbed up and took up position because all positions on the ground are made so that one needs to lie down during combat. Why would one stand up in combat in order to shoot? They are behind a shelter, and practically at ground level or maybe 50 centimetres up. It also fits within the 4 metre margin. There's a very slight difference in angle, if you move it half a metre up or down. It wouldn't result in much -- well, if we were to add 2 metres up and drew a line, it would also go through the area where we have the 4.2 metres. It is not linear. Only the angle is changed slightly. So whatever we take, it will always go below the ground of 4 metres. The altitude or the difference altitude is some 300 metres at 300 metres 1 or 2 metres have a very small impact on the margin of error. If the difference in altitude were 10 or 15 metres, then that would be much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So 10 metres could make the difference. Is that how I understand you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. If the ground was quite flat and the shooter was only 10 metres away, if the shooter's at 10 and the victim at zero, and then if we make the correction of 2 metres then the difference is great. But when the difference in altitude is 300 metres, then 1 or 2 metres result in a very small percentage, having a negligible impact on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If halfway there's an obstruction of 4 metres high, wouldn't it be fair to say that for the full length, it would be 8 metres? That's simple trigonometry, isn't it? I mean, if halfway is the obstruction - if you would please let me ask first - wouldn't it be true that then at full distance it would be 8 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the angle is 45 degrees. It depends on the angle. But that's what I was talking about. The difference in altitude of 300 metres reduces the impact of angle. How should I explain that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I simply ask you: If you draw a line, from A to B, and you draw another line, from A to a little bit above B, and if halfway the distance is 4 metres, irrespective of the angle, wouldn't it be true that, at the full distance, it would be 8 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That depends -- well, it can be calculated by using triangles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please prepare for me a little sketch in which halfway two lines have a difference of 4 metres, starting at the same point, and at the end, it's not 8 metres. If you would make such a sketch for me, I would appreciate that highly. If you need any specific -- any specific angles, et cetera, or -- I have -- and then please show it to me, I would be easily convinced if that's true. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. I'm looking at the clock. We're close to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only I have one question. Should be for this distance or some other distance? Or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I say if it's halfway 4 metres, then the full stretch, then it's 8 metres. That's the only thing I'm saying and that is irrespective of distance because that would be at least, in my view, but if the witness would convince me otherwise it makes no difference whether it's 200 metres, 500 metres or a kilometre. It's just like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move to another topic so we can go to the break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that a topic which you would deal with within five minutes or perhaps otherwise we would better take the break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to read from some transcripts as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps we take the break first and resume at quarter to 2.00. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question so it's clear to me, to make sure I understand you. So you had in mind the height of 4 and 8 metres irrespective of the distance. So at half the distance, the difference is 4 metres, and your question is: What is the difference at full length; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then it's fine. I'll prepare that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We'll take a break and we'll -- you may follow the usher, and we'll resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, were you able to make such a sketch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps put it on the ELMO. Yes, please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Upside down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't see anything at all. At this moment I see a box with -- a box with tissues. I think if we ... yes, there we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, thank you very much for doing it. Would you agree that the distance between A and D and B and C would also be the proportion of 1 to 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if I look carefully at your sketch, you would fully agree with me, which I said before, that if halfway, it is A, then the full way it's 2A. Which also means that if the obstacle halfway is 2 metres, then you would need, at the very end, 4 metres of difference in elevation to overcome it. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does that mean I should proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Mr. Lukic. I wouldn't have anyone else on my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll move now to F-3 incident from the 11th of July, 1993. And we need 1D05499 on our screens, page 88 in B/C/S and page 85 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Would Your Honours be inclined to receive this sketch made by Mr. Poparic as a Chamber's exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think, as a matter of fact, that as a result of the sketch, Mr. Poparic agreed fully with me that if it's halfway a certain distance then the full way, even if it is projected, doesn't make any -- angles is irrelevant, distance is irrelevant, it's just a double. And I think Mr. Poparic agreed with that so I don't need the sketch to have in evidence. It was just a means by which we could establish that we agreed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, indeed, he did. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, in this part of your report, in paragraph 45, you say that on the 11th of July, 1993 - actually you are dealing with this case - Munira Zametica was shot dead while collecting water from the Dobrinja river near the pedestrian bridge. In your view, what is characteristic of this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: According to the available documents, it is considered that Munira Zametica was shot from Dobrinja 4, an area that was under the control of the VRS and the distance was roughly 1100 metres away from where Munira Zametica was. What is characteristic is that there was shooting in Dobrinja practically all day and we don't have any precise information about the gun-fire involved. Further on, the time of the incident is in dispute. According to the police report, it was between 1900 hours and 1930. A lady neighbour who was with Munira Zametica claims that this happened earlier, and she was with Munira Zametica. She said during her testimony when it was just about to get dark, so this matches the police report but later on she corrected what she had said. Then, there is the death certificate from the hospital that refers to a different time, 1600 hours. And so on. The greatest problem here is to establish whether Munira Zametica was visible from the positions where she was shot from as it is claimed. There is another detail. What is claimed is that she was getting water from the Dobrinja river and that was shown in the film. The witness explained what was happening, that she was getting water from the river and that is absolutely impossible. There had to be some kind of steps so that she could go down to the water. Otherwise she couldn't have gotten any water and she could not have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, would you please stop the witness when he tells us whether there should have been steps, whether there -- whether there's any difference in times given by one witness according to the doctors. That's fully, but then fully, out of the scope of the witness's expertise. That's one. And, second, it's the task of the Chamber to do that. So would you please not present the witness in such a way that he tells us how we should do our job. Let him testify about what his expertise is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, he had to establish full details about every incident, and there were no traces like in mortar attacks, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All within his field of expertise, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His field --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not anywhere else. His expertise, how reliable hospital records are, whether one of the witnesses may have been mistaken, whether it was summertime, winter time, dark, all that is not within the expertise of this witness. So would you please stop him from doing that and would you please take him to what we are looking forward to, that is, the technical analysis in his expertise about whatever information would be there. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, time of the day is crucial for shooting. So he had to establish it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I gave you sufficient guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can establish that but with focussed questions, what is the difference between 4 and 4.30 in term of shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the bullets fly at one hour in summertime different at other times. Visibility is another matter. I don't know whether the witness is a expert in visibility, but I accept that as perhaps relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have quickly P01905 on our screens, please. Before we get it, I'll ask Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, do you know, you said that one woman was there with the late Munira Zametica? Do you know what his name was?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: I think her name is Sadija Sahinovic or something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you come closer to the microphone and speak into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have the testimony of Sadija Sahinovic before us now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... interpreters couldn't hear the name of the person who was with the deceased and that's why they're asking the witness to tell us -- come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I think that he said the same name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please repeat the name? What was the name of the lady?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Sadija Sahinovic was with Munira Zametica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you. [Interpretation] So what we need is page 5 in e-court. [In English] And line 3 -- actually line 2 the question was: "At the time that she was killed, what were you and she doing?" And in line 3, there is an answer. I quote: "We were on our way to get some water, and night was about to fall, and the river was exposed to sniper fire."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that's all we needed from this document. And can we now have P00973, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting for the report, you mentioned the police report. We are now going to get an Official Note of the Novi Grad public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 2 in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The penultimate paragraph, we see what is written there: "The murder took place on the 11 July 1993 between 1900 hours and 1930 hours, under the bridge over the Dobrinja river which connects the Dobrinja II and Dobrinja III." [In English] And now we'll have to see P00661, please. [Interpretation] We see this photograph. Mr. Poparic, can you recognise this place?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was taken from the bridge that is closer to Dobrinja IV and in the background we see the bridge underneath which Mrs. Munira Zametica was when she was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From where was this photograph taken? From the church or the side opposite the church?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: The church.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you try to go down to the river-bed to see whether water can be taken out of the river without having a ramp or something else to assist?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: Well, I had to be careful not to falling into the water. I didn't have a reserve pair of shoes so I didn't really go down to check whether this could be done. Well, one could go down here, but not with a bucket and water. But I mean, there's no way you can get water out of the river just with your hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you try that, with a bucket full of water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't try. I've already told you, it's so steep that I didn't dare go down without a bucket even, let alone with a bucket. Now, what is all of this about? What is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... no, no, no, sorry. I just wanted to know if you did that, and you said you didn't dare to do it and that's all. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is the place of the incident visible from the Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: It is, as we can see it in -- as can be seen in the picture. There are no obstacles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just check. The bridge before which is slowly bending, that's the bridge under which the -- Munira Zametica was shot at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is the bridge. And on it, you can see sandbags. Those sandbags were on both sides of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think you can proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On image 64, you marked a place under the bridge over the Dobrinja, and we need to go back to your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is 1D05499. Image 63 in the report. In the B/C/S, we need page 95; in the English, page 92. [In English] So we need lower photo from this page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see that the photograph was taken on September 17th, 2010 from the centre of the bridge beneath which Munira Zametica was shot. Who took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In front of us is the Orthodox church. We can see it. Four buildings are marked with numbers 1 through 4. Were there any other buildings next to the church in the territory controlled by the VRS from which the place of incident would be visible?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC
utterances.text: At that time building number 4 did not exist and the four crosses also marks four new buildings that did not exist at the time in Dobrinja IV controlled by the VRS. The buildings 1, 2 and 3, were in ABiH-controlled territory and existed at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question for clarification. The previous picture we saw, the bridge was sort of in an arc form. This one seems to be straight. Are we talking -- are these the same bridge or are they two different bridges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a different bridge. The bridge we saw on the previous photograph, the curved bridge, is the one that this photograph was taken from. So it's probably halfway or even closer to the church. In my assessment, it is about 400 metres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And between the two bridges, which one is it that it is alleged that she was shot under?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Munira Zametica was hurt under the bridge from which this photograph was taken. I stood on the bridge and took the photograph of the church. The other photograph was taken from the bridge we can see here with the red car on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I still don't understand. I'm not sure my question is answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we go back to image 59, the bridge where we see -- with the carpet, that is the bridge you can see in image 63, with the red car on it. So this was taken from another direction. I took image 63 from the curved bridge you can see in the background in image 59. You can see in image 59, there is no church in the background and in image 63 you can see the church. So the direction is opposite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I'm just concerned that the -- I'm just wondering whether the bridge suddenly becomes straight when it is taken from a different direction. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think it's time to adjourn. Witness, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. But before you leave the courtroom - and you may have heard this before - I instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 28th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
